title: Your Three-Story Interview Bank
subtitle: Prepare a compact set of truthful stories that can adapt to more than one question.
focus: Build three flexible examples: a change story, a problem-solving story and a learning story.
source_label: MIT Career Advising & Professional Development — STAR method

title: The Question Behind the Question
subtitle: Decode difficult prompts into the capability an interviewer is trying to assess.
focus: Identify the capability beneath a difficult interview question, then select evidence that demonstrates it honestly.
source_label: University of Michigan Career Center — Interviewing Resources

title: Research, Reflect, Rehearse
subtitle: Connect organisation research, your own evidence and natural spoken preparation.
focus: Create a preparation note that joins organisation signals, your relevant evidence and questions worth asking.
source_label: University of Michigan Career Center — Interviewing Resources

title: The Executive Screen
subtitle: Make the opening minutes of a recruiting or hiring-manager conversation easier to follow.
focus: Craft a concise, role-relevant opening that explains the operating situations you are prepared to lead through.
source_label: NYU Wasserman Center — Interviewing & Negotiation Process

title: When They Ask About a Failure
subtitle: Show ownership and learning without turning the story into blame or performance.
focus: Prepare a responsible answer that explains context, ownership, learning and what changed in your practice.
source_label: MIT Career Advising & Professional Development — STAR method

title: Questions That Help You Evaluate the Role
subtitle: Use interview questions to understand scope, success measures and decision rights.
focus: Build a question set that helps you assess the mandate, manager, decision rights and operating environment.
source_label: University of Michigan Career Center — Interviewing Resources

title: The Whole-Role Negotiation Map
subtitle: Evaluate the offer as a whole role, not only as a headline salary number.
focus: Compare compensation, benefits, scope, working conditions and decision criteria before you negotiate or decide.
source_label: DePaul Career Center — Job Offers & Salary Negotiation

title: Ask for Time Before You Answer
subtitle: Treat offer review as a deliberate professional decision rather than a rushed reaction.
focus: Create space to read an offer, identify information gaps and respond with clarity rather than urgency.
source_label: DePaul Career Center — Job Offers & Salary Negotiation

title: When Salary Cannot Move
subtitle: Clarify the overall package and ask responsibly without assuming every term is negotiable.
focus: Identify the one or two terms, questions or conditions that matter most when base salary has limited flexibility.
source_label: DePaul Career Center — Job Offers & Salary Negotiation

title: The Career Decision Memo
subtitle: Make the trade-offs visible before momentum makes the decision for you.
focus: Write a disciplined decision note that separates evidence, uncertainty, criteria and the next question.
source_label: DePaul Career Center — Job Offers & Salary Negotiation
